title: Unit and tower equations for normalized compact-support scalar comparisons
statement:
Let $K_0$ be a field, $X,Y$ finite-type $K_0$-schemes, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $K_0$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $K_0$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a compactification $c$ of $f$. At every finite subextension $A/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, use the derived-complete integral categories $\mathcal C_A^Z=D^b_c(Z,\mathcal O_A)$ and their raw Hom scalar localizations $\mathcal D_A^Z=D^b_c(Z,A)$, for $Z=X,Y$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Let $F_A:\mathcal C_A^X\to\mathcal C_A^Y$ and $G_A:\mathcal D_A^X\to\mathcal D_A^Y$ be the fixed normalized compact-support functors of [def-weil-compact-support-finite-action]: their objects are the values of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and $G_A(a\otimes v)=a\otimes F_A(v)$. Write $\widehat T^Z_{B/A}$ for completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $T^Z_{B/A}$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi].

Suppose the integral natural isomorphisms $b_{B/A}$ are the normalized strict-tower tensor-unit comparisons specified in [lem-weil-compact-support-normalized-scalar-isomorphisms], with their fixed derived-limit realization and full homotopy-category reduction normalization. Let $\beta_{B/A}:T^Y_{B/A}G_A\xrightarrow{\sim}G_BT^X_{B/A}$ be their raw localizations. Let $a^Z_{N,M,A}:T^Z_{N/M}T^Z_{M/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}T^Z_{N/A}$ and $e^Z_A:T^Z_{A/A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ be the canonical scalar associators and units [lem-weil-scalar-extension-composition].

For every finite $A\subseteq M\subseteq N$ in $\Omega$ and every $K\in\mathcal D_A^X$, the following equalities hold in the actual rational derived categories:
$$G_A(e^X_{A,K})\circ\beta_{A/A,K}=e^Y_{A,G_AK},$$
$$\beta_{N/A,K}\circ a^Y_{N,M,A,G_AK}
=G_N(a^X_{N,M,A,K})\circ\beta_{N/M,T^X_{M/A}K}\circ T^Y_{N/M}(\beta_{M/A,K}).$$
The equations concern precisely the prescribed tensor-unit mates and their fixed strict-tower realizations. They hold also for repeated fields. Only the unit and tower equations are asserted here.

source.place: First sentence, compatibility with composition: returned step 1 associator equation and identity-extension comparison only

proof.text:
Work on the ordinary derived categories of whole semilinear quotient systems. For $D=A,M,N$ write $\mathcal R_D,\mathcal L_D,H_D$ for coherent reduction, its fixed limit realization, and system compact support; write $S_i,U_i,\zeta_i$ for scalar extension, restriction and its unit for an inclusion $i$. The system-transpose normalization lemma identifies the prescribed $b_i$, under the fixed realization comparisons, with $\mathcal L(q_i)$. Its whole-system characterization is
$$U_i^Y(q_{i,L})\zeta^Y_{i,H_DL}=d_{i,S_i^XL}H_D(\zeta^X_{i,L}).$$
The relevant Hom bijection is on $\mathscr D_B^Y=D(\text{strict }R_{B,\bullet}\text{-systems})$, for every derived target. It is not the quotient-level bijection of the hypothesis node. The same lemma identifies the coherent mixed units with these scalar units via $s_W$. We shall prove the equations for these $q_i$ before applying any realization.

source.place: First sentence, replace the returned finite-level uniqueness argument by the whole-system transpose characterization

proof.text:
Put $i:A\to M$, $j:M\to N$, $k=ji$. The restriction-cocycle lemma gives, under $U_iU_j=U_k$,
$$d_k=U_i^Y(d_j)\,d_iU_j^X,$$
and gives identity restriction comparison for an identity inclusion. Its hypotheses hold for the same-index valuation quotient sequences: each ring is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, and the inclusions commute with quotient transitions. For ramified inclusions $\varpi_A^{n+1}$ maps into $(\varpi_M^{n+1})$, so the quotient maps used here exist; their flatness is not required. All equalities in this step are equalities of derived-system transformations.

Let $a_S^W:S_j^WS_i^W\cong S_k^W$ and $e_S^W:S_{A/A}^W\cong1$ be the unit-normalized scalar associator and unitor on the ringed sequence site. The scalar-coherence lemma supplies their derived left-adjoint uniqueness normalization: the associator carries the composite adjunction unit to the direct unit, and the unitor carries the identity-extension unit to identity. Thus on whole systems
$$U_k^W(a_S^W)\,U_i^W(\zeta_j^W S_i^W)\,\zeta_i^W=\zeta_k^W,\qquad e_S^W\zeta_{A/A}^W=1.$$
The scalar adjunction on the sequence site gives the composite Hom bijection explicitly: first transpose along $S_j\dashv U_j$, then along $S_i\dashv U_i$. Its value at $h:S_jS_iP\to Z$ is $U_iU_j(h)\,U_i(\zeta_{j,S_iP})\,\zeta_{i,P}$, by naturality of the units. Both are bijections for every $Z$, so their composite is injective. On coherent reduction inputs, the mixed-unit composition lemma and Step 1 identify these units and structural maps with the prescribed completed ones.

source.place: First sentence, iterated whole-system scalar unit and explicit composite Hom bijection

proof.text:
Fix $L\in\mathscr D_A^X$. Compare maps from $S_j^YS_i^YH_AL$ to $H_NS_k^XL$:
$$P=q_{k,L}a^Y_{S,H_AL},\qquad Q=H_N(a^X_{S,L})q_{j,S_i^XL}S_j^Y(q_{i,L}).$$
Transpose along the composite Hom bijection of Step 3. Its value at $P$ is $U_k^Y(q_{k,L})\zeta^Y_{k,H_AL}$, because the source associator carries the iterated unit to $\zeta_k^Y$. For $Q$, naturality of $\zeta_j^Y$ moves $q_{i,L}$ through that unit. Insert the defining equation for $q_j$, then that for $q_i$. Naturality of $d_i$ for $\zeta^X_{j,S_i^XL}$ gives the transpose
$$U_k^Y(H_N(a^X_{S,L}))\,U_i^Y(d_{j,S_j^XS_i^XL})\,d_{i,U_j^XS_j^XS_i^XL}\,H_A\bigl(U_i^X(\zeta^X_{j,S_i^XL})\zeta^X_{i,L}\bigr).$$
Here each $d$ is evaluated at the displayed system object. This is a calculation in the system categories using their adjunctions, not a lift of calculations at the indices $n$.

source.place: First sentence, whole-system transposition of the two tower routes

proof.text:
Step 2 combines the middle two restriction factors in the last display into $d_{k,S_j^XS_i^XL}$. Naturality of $d_k$ for $a^X_{S,L}$ then makes that display
$$d_{k,S_k^XL}\,H_A\bigl(U_k^X(a^X_{S,L})U_i^X(\zeta^X_{j,S_i^XL})\zeta^X_{i,L}\bigr)
=d_{k,S_k^XL}H_A(\zeta^X_{k,L}).$$
This is the transpose of $P$ by Step 1. Injectivity of the composite system Hom bijection proves $P=Q$ in $\mathscr D_N^Y$. For an identity inclusion transpose $H_A(e^X_{S,L})q_{A/A,L}$: Step 1, the identity case of Step 2 and the unit equation of Step 3 give $1_{H_AL}$. The transpose of $e^Y_{S,H_AL}$ is also $1_{H_AL}$. The single system Hom bijection proves the unit equality there as well.

source.place: First sentence, injectivity on system Hom sets proves the tower and identity equations

proof.text: Realize the equalities of Steps 4-5 on $L=\mathcal R_A^XK$. By the system-transpose normalization lemma, each prescribed $b$ is the limit of its $q$ under the fixed operation/scalar counit identifications. In the iterated route insert the counits $\epsilon_M:\mathcal R_M\mathcal L_M\to1$ at the intermediate systems. DVR effectivity makes every evaluation an isomorphism; joint conservativity of system evaluation then makes these counits invertible on the normalized systems. Naturality $\epsilon_V\,\mathcal R_M\mathcal L_M(h)=h\,\epsilon_U$ moves each $q$ through its adjacent counit; each intermediate counit cancels its inverse. Thus realization of $Q$ is precisely $F_N(a^X_K)b_{N/M,C^X_{M/A}K}C^Y_{N/M}(b_{M/A,K})$, and realization of $P$ is $b_{N/A,K}a^Y_{F_AK}$. The coherent scalar reduction model identifies successive scalar realizations with the direct one using tensor association on whole quotient systems. The completed scalar-coherence lemma identifies its associator and unitor with the stated completed maps and, after rationalization, with $a^W,e^W$. Applying the limit functor therefore proves both integral equations for the fixed maps. This uses the stated identification of the actual $b$ with its realization, not just the equation for $\mathcal R_B(b)$ and not faithfulness of finite evaluation.

source.place: First sentence, fixed counit-normalized realization of the system equalities

proof.text: Apply raw Hom scalar localization. It preserves identities and composition, has the same objects as the integral category, and sends $b$ to the prescribed $\beta$. The actual rational compact-support action is $G_D(t\otimes v)=t\otimes F_D(v)$. The integral equations of Step 6 therefore become exactly the two rational equations in the statement, for every rational object $K$. The scalar associators and unitors rationalize to those of the question. Repeated fields were allowed in the system-unit and restriction identities, so both equations include all repeated-field cases.

source.place: First sentence, raw localization of the established integral equations
